title: Closed-fibre injectivity puts the tensor kernel in the extended maximal ideal
statement: Let A₀,A be commutative local rings, B,C commutative rings, and let α:A₀→A be local and induce a surjection on residue fields. Give A and C A₀-algebra structures agreeing with α and a ring map γ:A₀→C. Let φ:A→B and ψ:C→B be ring maps, D=C⊗[A₀]A [def-weil-module-base-change], and F:D→B a ring map satisfying F(c⊗a)=ψ(c)φ(a). Suppose ker(C→B→B/(m_A B))=m₀C, with the first map ψ and m₀C extended along γ. Then ker F⊆m_A D, where m_A is extended by a↦1⊗a. No flatness or surjectivity of F is assumed.

source.place: Remark 07NS (4), closed-fibre isomorphism; Proposition 07NQ, kernel-tensor paragraph. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NS and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NQ.

proof.text: Let D=C⊗[A₀]A, i(a)=1⊗a, j(c)=c⊗1, L=m_A D, and J=m_A B. Balancing gives j(c γ(r))=c⊗α(r). The pure-tensor formula implies F(L)⊆J. Locality of α and balancing imply j(m₀C)⊆L; both assertions follow from Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap on the respective ideal generators.

For each a∈A lift its residue through the surjective residue-field map and then through A₀→k₀, obtaining r∈A₀ with a−α(r)∈m_A. Thus c⊗a−j(cγ(r))=(c⊗1)(1⊗(a−α(r))) lies in L. Tensor induction, including zero and sums, proves every x∈D has x−j(c)∈L for some c∈C.

If F(x)=0, applying F to x−j(c)∈L gives −ψ(c)∈J, hence ψ(c)∈J. The assumed kernel equality implies c∈m₀C; consequently j(c)∈L. Add x−j(c)∈L to conclude x∈L. Flatness and surjectivity of F are not required.
